scheme_name: Financial Assistance To Non-School Going Disabled Children Scheme
description:
The Financial Assistance to Non-School Going Disabled Children Scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to provide financial support to families with disabled children who are not enrolled in formal educational institutions. 

This scheme was introduced in 2009 as part of the broader efforts to enhance the welfare of disabled individuals in the country. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to ensure that families with disabled children receive the necessary financial assistance to support their children's needs. 

The scheme aims to provide a monthly financial assistance of ₹1,500 to eligible families. 

This amount is intended to help cover various expenses related to the care and development of disabled children who are not attending school. 

The scheme targets children with disabilities aged between 0 to 18 years. 

To qualify for the assistance, the child must have a disability that is certified by a competent authority. 

The disability must be defined according to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. 

This Act recognizes various types of disabilities including blindness, low vision, leprosy cured persons, hearing impairment, locomotor disability, mental illness, and multiple disabilities. 

Families applying for assistance must meet specific income criteria. 

The annual family income must not exceed ₹2,00,000. 

This income limit is set to ensure that the assistance reaches the most economically disadvantaged families. 

The application process for the scheme involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must obtain a disability certificate for the child from a recognized medical authority. 

This certificate must clearly state the nature and extent of the disability. 

Next, the family must fill out the application form for the scheme. 

The application form can be obtained from the local office of the Department of Social Welfare or downloaded from the official government website. 

Along with the application form, the family must submit several documents. 

These documents include proof of income such as income tax returns or salary slips. 

A copy of the child's disability certificate must also be included. 

Additionally, proof of residence such as an Aadhaar card or utility bill is required. 

Once the application is complete with all necessary documents, it must be submitted to the local Social Welfare Department. 

The department will then verify the application and documents submitted. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the bank account of the applicant. 

The disbursement is made on a monthly basis. 

The scheme is implemented through the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment at the central level. 

At the state level, the respective Departments of Social Welfare are responsible for the execution of the scheme. 

Families can contact the local Social Welfare Department for any queries regarding the application process. 

The contact details for the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of government initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life for disabled individuals. 

It aligns with the National Policy for Persons with Disabilities, which emphasizes the need for inclusive education and social support. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹300 crores for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2022-2023. 

This funding is aimed at reaching approximately 20,000 families across the country. 

The scheme is particularly significant in rural areas where access to educational facilities for disabled children is limited. 

It recognizes the challenges faced by families in providing care and support for their disabled children. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is intended to alleviate some of the economic burdens faced by these families. 

The scheme also aims to encourage families to invest in the health and well-being of their disabled children. 

By providing financial support, the government hopes to promote better living conditions and opportunities for disabled children. 

The monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted periodically to assess its impact and effectiveness. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme and address any challenges faced during implementation. 

The scheme has been positively received by many families who have benefited from the financial assistance. 

It has helped in meeting the basic needs of disabled children, including healthcare, nutrition, and rehabilitation. 

The government continues to advocate for the rights of disabled individuals through various programs and policies. 

The Financial Assistance to Non-School Going Disabled Children Scheme is a crucial step in this direction. 

It reflects the government's commitment to social justice and equality for all citizens. 

In summary, the Financial Assistance to Non-School Going Disabled Children Scheme is a vital welfare initiative aimed at supporting families with disabled children who are not enrolled in formal education. 

With a monthly assistance of ₹1,500, the scheme provides essential financial support to help cover the costs associated with caring for disabled children. 

The eligibility criteria focus on age, disability certification, and income limits to ensure that the assistance reaches those who need it most. 

The application process is straightforward, requiring necessary documentation and submission to the local Social Welfare Department. 

The scheme is implemented at both central and state levels, with a significant budget allocation to support its objectives. 

Through this initiative, the government seeks to enhance the quality of life for disabled children and their families across India.
